dimensions.label: Stage & Hiring Pressure
dimensions.description: Clear growth or expansion signal, active technical hiring, and enough funding, revenue, or customer pressure to support engineering headcount.

levels.0: No credible company, team, or hiring capacity signal.
levels.1: Speculative team, unclear budget, or mostly founder-only activity.
levels.2: Early or unstable company with weak evidence of engineering hiring capacity.
levels.3: Company looks viable, but current hiring pressure is unknown.
levels.4: Healthy company with visible technical hiring, but urgency or headcount expansion is less clear.
levels.5: Clear growth or expansion signal, active technical hiring, and enough funding, revenue, or customer pressure to support engineering headcount.

dimensions.label: Team Composition
dimensions.description: Engineering-led team with visible founders or early engineers in AI systems, infrastructure, data, research, or strong product engineering.

levels.0: No visible technical team behind a technical claim.
levels.1: Very little visible technical talent, or engineering appears outsourced.
levels.2: Business, consulting, sales, or operations appear to dominate; engineering may be secondary.
levels.3: Technical team exists, but technical leadership or depth is not yet clear.
levels.4: Clear technical leadership and enough visible engineers to support serious system-building.
levels.5: Engineering-led team with visible founders or early engineers in AI systems, infrastructure, data, research, or strong product engineering.

dimensions.label: Technical Closure
dimensions.description: Company appears to own meaningful system layers: product, data, retrieval, eval, runtime, model, infrastructure, or production feedback loop.

levels.1: Thin wrapper, prompt studio, or demo-heavy product with weak durable engineering asset signal.
levels.2: Mainly integration, implementation, or services around third-party platforms.
levels.3: Product has real technical content, but closure vs. wrapper/delivery model needs more evidence.
levels.4: Strong in-house engineering exists, but one important technical layer or long-term moat is still uncertain.
levels.5: Company appears to own meaningful system layers: product, data, retrieval, eval, runtime, model, infrastructure, or production feedback loop.

dimensions.label: Domain Alignment
dimensions.description: Directly matches AI agent systems, agent infrastructure, memory/retrieval, eval, runtime, observability, AI tooling, or production AI workflows.

levels.0: No meaningful alignment with the target direction.
levels.1: Weak fit with only surface-level AI branding.
levels.2: Some technical relevance, but mostly outside the target direction.
levels.3: General AI/data/product engineering fit, but not clearly close to agent systems or infrastructure.
levels.4: Strong adjacent fit: workflow automation, data infrastructure, LLMOps/MLOps, voice AI infrastructure, or full-stack AI product engineering.
levels.5: Directly matches AI agent systems, agent infrastructure, memory/retrieval, eval, runtime, observability, AI tooling, or production AI workflows.

dimensions.label: Culture & Ownership Signal
dimensions.description: Public signals show engineering ownership, technical taste, high standards, and room for individual judgment.

levels.0: Clear chaos, exploitation, or bad-faith culture signal.
levels.1: High-agency language likely means unclear scope, low support, or exploitative pace.
levels.2: Signals suggest delivery pressure, sales-led priority churn, or weak technical decision rights.
levels.3: Culture is not clearly bad, but ownership and engineering quality are unknown.
levels.4: Builder culture or strong technical voice is visible, with manageable unknowns.
levels.5: Public signals show engineering ownership, technical taste, high standards, and room for individual judgment.

dimensions.label: Right to Work & Location
dimensions.description: Location and employment setup clearly match a viable right-to-work path.

levels.1: Company likely cannot support the needed path, but a personal alternative may exist.
levels.2: Feasibility is weak and would require non-standard sponsorship, relocation, or contract conversion.
levels.3: Location looks plausible, but right-to-work route is unknown.
levels.4: Likely feasible, but entity, remote setup, sponsorship, or start timing needs confirmation.
levels.5: Location and employment setup clearly match a viable right-to-work path.

dimensions.label: Reachability Signal
dimensions.description: Clear reachable surface exists: engineering founders, hiring managers, recruiters, OSS/community presence, events, or warm network paths.

levels.0: No practical way to monitor or reach the target.
levels.1: Hard to identify anyone relevant, and no hiring or community surface is visible.
levels.2: Few visible people or weak contact surface.
levels.3: Reachability unknown; company can be watched but needs contact research.
levels.4: Some reachable people or community surfaces are visible.
levels.5: Clear reachable surface exists: engineering founders, hiring managers, recruiters, OSS/community presence, events, or warm network paths.

decisionThresholds.label: Priority Target
decisionThresholds.action: Track actively, identify people, monitor roles, and prepare tailored positioning.

decisionThresholds.label: Qualified Watch
decisionThresholds.action: Keep on watchlist and refresh evidence periodically.

decisionThresholds.label: Low Priority
decisionThresholds.action: Do not actively pursue unless new evidence appears.
